name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,198

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One playing music live breaking into Gipsy Kings’ The Mountain

indicators.note: something breaking into a pair forces its way between them, so the verb sits inside the other pieces

blocks.note: a disc jockey plays music
to live is to be, to exist
the Gipsy Kings sing in Spanish, whose word for 'the' is el

explanation.surface: A live musician gatecrashes a Gipsy Kings song called The Mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gipsy Kings are a French flamenco-pop band singing in Spanish, so their 'The' is the Spanish article.
explanation.definitionFit: A djebel is a hill or mountain in North Africa and the Middle East, from the Arabic word.

clue.text: Knife with sort of strap, note, attached to limb

blocks.note: a jockstrap is a sort of strap
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: Someone describes a knife sheathed on a strap fastened to the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockteleg is a Scots word for a clasp knife or large pocket knife.

clue.text: The Bar having position for magistrate, historically

blocks.note: a bail is a bar, such as one separating horses in a stable or across cricket stumps
the lie of something is its position

explanation.surface: The legal Bar is given a place in appointing magistrates, in times past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Bar' suggests barristers, but here it is just a bar of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A baillie was a Scottish municipal magistrate, an office now largely ceremonial and so historical.

clue.text: Where grouse are ostentatious, moose buries head

indicators.note: the leading letter is pushed down and buried among the letters that follow it

blocks.note: the elk is the European name for the moose

explanation.surface: A moose hides its head, unlike showy grouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The E at the front of ELK drops one place, between L and K.
explanation.definitionFit: A lek is the ground where male grouse gather to strut and display to females.

clue.text: Anoraks go wrong with us and leak

indicators.note: things that go wrong get mixed up, so the letters here are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Our anoraks fail and let the rain in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go wrong' looks like part of the story about faulty raincoats, but 'wrong' is the signal and 'go' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Kagoules are lightweight hooded waterproof jackets, the same garment as anoraks.

clue.text: Plug in kettle at first, smashing pot

indicators.note: one item goes in another, so the plug sits inside the remaining letters
at first points to the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the opening letter of kettle
an ad is a plug, a piece of publicity
smashing means first-rate, A1, written here with the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone plugs in the kettle and then breaks a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means excellent; in crosswords the digit 1 often becomes the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A kadai, or karahi, is a deep round Indian cooking vessel like a wok.

clue.text: Series of upcoming features: in it a legendary glue maker

indicators.note: a series is a run of consecutive letters lifted out of the words that follow
in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: A trailer for coming features promises a legendary glue maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Read upwards, the letters hidden across 'features: in it a leg' spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelatiniser turns substances into gelatin, the basis of animal glue, so it makes glue.

clue.text: In some places, peel off turnips scattered

indicators.note: scattered things are thrown about, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Here and there, someone peels turnips scattered about the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In some places' marks the definition as dialect, not a location in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstrip is a dialect verb meaning to strip or undress, taking something off completely.

clue.text: A pony, perhaps, or one nearly two thirds spent?

blocks.note: first meaning: a member of the horse family, of which the pony is one example
second meaning, playful: a pound with an electronic prefix, as money spent online

explanation.walkthrough: A pony is also slang for twenty-five pounds, so the whole clue hints at money; the second part plays on the answer splitting as E plus QUID, a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Any animal of the horse family, Equidae, including horses, asses and zebras, is called this.

clue.text: Did as one urging horse maybe has done, taking chestnut for canter, finally

definitions.text: Did as one urging horse maybe

indicators.note: taking one thing for another swaps it in where the other stood
finally picks the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: to be done is to be cheated or tricked
CH is the standard abbreviation for chestnut, a horse colour
the closing letter of canter

explanation.surface: A rider urged the horse on, a chestnut breaking into a canter at last.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of TRICKED is replaced with CH.
explanation.definitionFit: To tchick is to make a clicking sound with the tongue, as riders do to urge a horse on.

clue.text: Movements in Hungary and America female fronts

indicators.note: to front something is to stand before it, so the woman's word comes first

blocks.note: a lass is a girl or young woman
the United States

explanation.surface: A woman leads political movements in Hungary and the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movements' suggests politics; here it means sections of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A lassu is the slow opening section of a Hungarian csárdás dance, so these are musical movements.

clue.text: See the other side in case involving graduate, current holder of particular world view

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up within, so the outer phrase surrounds what follows

blocks.note: PTO, please turn over, is printed to tell readers to see the other side
lest means in case, for fear that
a Master of Arts is a graduate
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A graduate sees both sides of a case concerning the current holder of a worldview.
explanation.walkthrough: 'world view' is literal: the Ptolemaic system put the Earth at the centre of the universe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ptolemaist believes in Ptolemy's earth-centred model of the cosmos, a particular picture of the universe.

clue.text: Disturbed youth simply overwhelmed by crooked dame

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of true, so the letters are twisted into a new order
to be overwhelmed is to be engulfed, so these words go inside the other piece

blocks.note: a lad is a youth
just means simply, merely
taken as written

explanation.surface: A troubled boy is simply overpowered by a dishonest older woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone maladjusted is psychologically troubled and unable to cope with their surroundings, as disturbed suggests.

clue.text: Order from Balmoral enacted again, I must depart

indicators.note: departing means leaving, so that letter is taken away from the word

blocks.note: to enact again is to redo; past tense
taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal decree from Balmoral is passed again, and someone must leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral is the royal castle in Scotland, signalling a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Redd is a Scots verb meaning to put in order or tidy up, so order is a verb.

clue.text: Kind old lady will ask niece to leave tips

indicators.note: tips are the ends of things, here the closing letters of each word

blocks.note: the closing letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A kindly old lady asks her niece to hand out tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind old lady' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'old', which marks an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ylke is an old spelling of ilk, meaning a sort or type, as in people of that ilk.

clue.text: Responsibility ultimately rests on church, in trouble about prayers

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, picking the closing letter
in an across answer, resting on something means following it
about means turned round, so the word for trouble is read backwards
the first group of pieces goes in the turned-round word

blocks.note: the closing letter of responsibility
CH is the standard abbreviation for church
naps are short rests
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: The buck stops with the church, which is in difficulties over its prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lychnapsia are evening prayers in the Greek Orthodox church, said at the lamp-lighting hour.

clue.text: Caught a whiff of someone climbing mount

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters run upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
BO, body odour, is an unpleasant personal whiff

explanation.surface: A climber's body odour is noticed on the mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' looks like a hill but here it is something you ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A cob is a sturdy short-legged horse, and a mount is any animal you ride.

clue.text: Resident lifted blue nickel tablet in each hand

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means raised up, so those letters read from bottom to top
the tablet goes in between the two hands

blocks.note: blue means smutty, lewd
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel
left and right, one for each hand
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A resident raises a blue nickel-plated tablet in each hand.
explanation.definitionFit: An indweller is someone who dwells in a place, an inhabitant or resident.

clue.text: Second serious physical injury’s stopped by one with posh daggers

indicators.note: something stopped up is plugged, so the following pieces fill a gap inside it

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
GBH, grievous bodily harm, with the 's
the Roman numeral for one
and means with, together with
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A second victim is seriously hurt by an upper-class thug carrying daggers.
explanation.walkthrough: GBH is the British legal term for a serious assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A sgian dubh is the small dagger worn tucked into the sock with Highland dress.

clue.text: Log supporter’s offer to East London club

indicators.note: the Cockney accent of East London famously drops its aitches

blocks.note: to hand something to someone is to offer it
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A fan of a log-burning stove offers money to an East London football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East London club' suggests a football team such as West Ham, but East London only drops the H.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron is a metal stand on a hearth that holds the logs up in an open fire.

clue.text: So prudish, oddly concealed sources from history

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are hidden away, leaving only the even ones

blocks.note: the even-placed letters of these words

explanation.surface: Historians, being prudish, hid away their sources.
explanation.definitionFit: Ord is an old word for a point or beginning, so ords are origins in archaic English.

clue.text: Float having nothing to tie it

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to rope is to tie
it means sex appeal, SA

explanation.surface: A float with nothing to tie it down drifts off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal is an old crossword convention giving SA.
explanation.definitionFit: An oropesa is a torpedo-shaped float used to tow a minesweeping cable.

clue.text: Knight the last character to reflect ancient curse

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
to dub someone is to knight them

explanation.surface: A knight, the last of his line, thinks on an ancient curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight' looks like a noun, giving N or K, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Zbud, a shortening of God's blood, was an old oath, so it is an archaic curse.

clue.text: Right away, bra shed to reveal chest

indicators.note: right is R, and sending it away removes that letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a shed is a hut

explanation.surface: A bra comes off at once to reveal a chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bra shed' looks like an undressing verb, but shed is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A bahut is an ornamental cabinet or chest, the word borrowed from French furniture.

clue.text: Drug received corrupted young prince

blocks.note: an upper is a stimulant drug
roger is radio talk for message received

explanation.surface: A young prince is corrupted by drugs he was given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received corrupted' reads like an anagram signal, but both words belong elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper roger was old thieves' slang for a rogue of good birth, a young gentleman gone bad.

clue.text: Image by artist that would start a movement?

blocks.note: pic is short for picture
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist

explanation.surface: A picture by an artist launches an art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The movement is not artistic but a bowel movement, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Picra, or hiera picra, is a purgative powder of aloes and canella, a laxative.

clue.text: Cricketer holding firm, mostly, for India

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is lost
holding means gripping inside, so the cricketer surrounds the firm word

blocks.note: a bat is a batsman
firm means hard

explanation.surface: A batsman stands firm for the Indian team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' suggests a company; here it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Bharat is the Hindi name for India, used in its constitution alongside the English name.

clue.text: With swelling around sole trousers are annoying

indicators.note: used as a verb, to trouser is to pocket, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: C is short for circa, around
sole means only
to vex is to annoy

explanation.surface: Swollen soles make trousers a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like clothing but is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Convexly means in a curving outward way, bulging, and so with a swelling shape.

clue.text: Some number of letters between DG and church body once

blocks.note: N stands for an unspecified number
the letters that come after D and before G in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A few letters pass between the Director-General and the church authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: DG looks like an abbreviation for Director-General, but here the two letters are alphabet bookends.
explanation.definitionFit: Nef is an obsolete form of nave, the main body of a church building.

clue.text: Breathers help at home, with the rest having withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the whole sequence runs backwards

blocks.note: aid is help
in means at home
etc, et cetera, means and the rest

explanation.surface: Helpers at home take breaks while everyone else retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathers' suggests rests, but it means organs that breathe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ctenidia are the comb-like gills of molluscs, the organs they use to take in oxygen.

clue.text: Brotherhood ducks out of supporting a Conservative

indicators.note: the named letters go out of the phrase, being removed from it

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O
to be for something is to support it
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A brotherhood refuses to back a Conservative candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: A fratry is a fraternity or convent of friars, a religious brotherhood.
